extraction.name: LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data
extraction.description: LUMA is a unique multimodal dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It extends the CIFAR 10/100 dataset with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model. The dataset enables the controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty to achieve and tailor specific experiments and benchmarking initiatives.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Foumier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Foumier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR ’25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from multiple sources. Images were taken from CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Audio samples were extracted from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora, with additional voluntary contributions from colleagues. Text data was generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model. The modalities were aligned such that each text passage relates to the object in the corresponding image, and each audio recording is the pronunciation of the object label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from CIFAR-10/100; Audio from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice, and voluntary contributions; Text generated by Gemma-7B Instruct LLM.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes a Python package that allows for the injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties. This includes controlling data diversity, adding different types of real-world noise (background noise for audio, keyboard/OCR/spelling noise for text, Gaussian/blur/noise for images), label noise (reassigning labels based on semantic proximity), and injecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were selected from CIFAR-10/100. Audio samples were extracted using forced alignments (Montreal Forced Aligner) or existing alignments, then validated automatically using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model. Samples failing automatic validation were manually validated using Label Studio. Text samples were generated by Gemma-7B, validated by masking labels and re-classifying with the same model, and filtered for bias using the Gemma model. Biased texts for specific classes were regenerated with modified prompts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Audio samples were annotated by 17 annotators (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge. Annotators answered 'Yes' or 'No' to whether the audio said the word below. Two annotations were collected per sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. Text samples were validated using an automated pipeline involving the Gemma-7B model for classification and bias detection.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation agreement was 71.61%. Only samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted. Conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model, Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model, Label Studio
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available as a Python package and on Hugging Face. The code and instructions are open-source on GitHub. The authors plan to include dependent modalities in the future.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Audio samples contain voices of volunteer contributors and colleagues. These were anonymized and trimmed before inclusion.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches, particularly for safety-critical applications like healthcare and autonomous driving. It aims to help the research community design more trustworthy machine learning approaches.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The text generation process introduced gender bias for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'. The authors detected this using the Gemma model and attempted to mitigate it by reconstructing prompts with specific topics and keywords, though some bias remained. The dataset may also contain factual inaccuracies due to LLM generation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is not intended to be used as a source of knowledge or information due to potential factual inaccuracies and biases in the generated text. The baseline models provided are not intended to be state-of-the-art but serve as a starting point. The audio data may contain noise from forced alignments. The text data is generated and may not reflect real-world linguistic diversity perfectly.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking of multimodal deep learning algorithms, specifically for uncertainty quantification and robustness evaluation.
